statement: Pushing back on a student's plan to keep only 1000 keys in memory, the teacher said there is no reason to limit memory to 1000 keys: far more keys can be kept in memory.
detail: This comes just before the teacher calls the B+ tree / 8 KB block proposal over-engineering. It anticipates the later estimate that the whole index (about 1.75 MB) fits in RAM.
speaker: teacher
verbatim: why only 1000 keys in memory? So I can keep a lot.
flags: check: speaker of "So I can keep a lot" (may be Student 2 replying; the teacher continues "No, why I'm saying this is")
